These aren't signs of a mature worldchanging technology, but the signs of an industry running on the hype and investor cash. Many AI startups are being valued at hundreds of millions of dollars but are still yet to make any profit. Some economists are claiming that the value of tech companies like Microsoft, Meta, and Nvidia have become completely detached from reality. One Wall Street expert wrote chillingly that the difference between the IT bubble in the '90s and the AI bubble today is that the top 10 companies in the S&P 500 today are more overvalued than they were in the '90s. So, while it might be tempting to single out Apple's lack of AI innovation as a massive mistake and point to the iPhone as evidence of issues that cut right to the heart of the company, the issue might actually be much bigger than that. The truth is the entire tech industry is gambling on AI. It doesn't matter if you're a backer or a skeptic. This is a new frontier for big tech and no one can predict its future. The iPhone event just revealed some of the conflicts facing the tech industry. Do you invest in AI? Do you wait? There are probably no right or wrong answers here. Whether Apple has backed itself into a corner or is right to be avoiding AI completely, time will only tell, but the stakes will be clear.
